title: Rollout observability handoff — midweek notes
content:
Context: quick midweek sync focused on observability handoff for the new rollout pipeline (panel v3). Primary goal is to make the canary signals actionable for on-call and the rollout owner without adding noise to the console.

Attendees: Aisha (owner), Miguel, Ravi, Lena, Priya, Evan (ops carve-in)

Meeting format: 15m standup + 20m signal triage (this doc captures highlights, decisions, and action items).

Summary / Why this matters
- panel v3 rollouts will be routed via the new "circuit" policy; if we don't tighten observability, engineering and SRE will see lots of false positives.
- Need deterministic alerting thresholds that map to rollback criteria in the rollout runbook.

What we reviewed
1) Canary metrics baseline
   - Latency p50/p95 for panel fetch flows (ui-panel-api -> panel-cache) measured on synthetic traffic: p50 62ms, p95 210ms.
   - Token-generation tail (streaming responses) artifact: p99 increased by 320ms in one run; correlated with larger KV cache misses.
   - Error rate: upstream 5xx rate on canary traffic 0.12% vs baseline 0.03% (small but noticeable spike during cold-starts).

2) New dashboard tiles
   - Added "canary delta" view that shows rolling ratio of canary vs baseline across latency, errors, and embedding similarity drift.
   - Quick filter for customer-impacting routes (routes with external traffic > 5rps).

3) Alerting prototype
   - Two alert classes proposed:
     a) SLO breach alert: triggers when canary p95 > baseline p95 by > 40% for 5m and traffic > 10rps. Severity: P1 (auto pause rollout).
     b) Noise guard alert: triggers when absolute canary error rate > 0.5% for 3m. Severity: P2 (manual review).
   - Decision: implement both, but attach immediate auto-pause only to the SLO breach alert. Noise guard will create an incident only if sustained for 15m.

Open questions noted
- Drift measurement: how to measure quality drift for non-deterministic LLM outputs? Priya proposed using embedding-similarity with a small labeled prompt set; Miguel suggested adding a cheap reranker to flag semantic regressions. Need to pick one MVP.
- Should auto-pause be global or per-route? Current approach: per-route auto-pause, with an emergency global kill switch for severe incidents.

Action items (owner — ETA)
- Miguel: wire "canary delta" panel into the rollout UI and add the per-route quick filter (PR#4120). ETA: 2027-02-21.
- Priya: prototype embedding-similarity drift check using 50 canonical prompts + faiss-lite index; report false-positive rate. ETA: 2027-02-23.
- Ravi: implement alert rules in staging (SLO breach + noise guard), connect to test pager via ops escalation. ETA: 2027-02-19.
- Lena: update rollout runbook to include new pause criteria and explicit per-route mitigation checklist (what to check: logs, kv-cache hit rate, model variant fallback). ETA: 2027-02-20.
- Aisha: schedule a 30m dry-run (synthetic traffic replay) with SRE to exercise auto-pause and rollback behavior. Proposed window: 2027-02-22 04:00-04:30 PT. Confirmed: tentative.

Triage notes from the signal session
- Observed a repeatable p99 spike when sequence length > 1024 on a specific shard. Root cause hypothesis: kernel dispatch path chooses non-quantized routine under memory pressure.
- Short-term mitigation: add shard-level capacity buffer in the routing policy; next deploy will reserve 10% spare capacity for canaries. Action: Ravi to update routing policy config (ETA 2027-02-19).
- Long-term: research quantization/path selection heuristics (tracked in JIRA-7428 assigned to infra-ops team).

Runbook clarifications (explicit phrasing we agreed to add)
- "Pause rollout" = set rollout state to PAUSED + notify rollout channel + create incident link in console.
- "Auto-pause" requires: canary p95 > baseline p95 by 40% for 5m AND canary traffic >= 10rps.
- Manual rollback checklist: (1) switch to previous stable model variant; (2) toggle cache warmup mode; (3) if embed drift present, switch to baseline reranker.

Notes to self / rough ideas
- Consider a lightweight RTT heatmap per route; could make triage faster than looking at raw p95 numbers.
- Add a 'confidence' score to canary delta so SRE can tune alert thresholds per customer tier.
- If embedding-sim drift proves noisy, fall back to "semantic smoke tests" (hand-labeled QA set) run every 30m.

Post-meeting decisions
- Implement the two-tier alert model (SLO breach auto-pause + noise guard for ops review).
- Proceed with embedding-similarity MVP for quality drift (Priya) but gate global auto-rollback on validated low-FPR.

Follow-ups / next sync
- Dry-run with SRE (Aisha, Ravi, Miguel, Priya) on 2027-02-22 04:00 PT.
- Review embedding-sim prototype in weekly analytics sync (2027-02-24 standup).
- Next short update: 2027-02-19 (implementation progress check).

Misc
- Slack threads referenced: #rollouts-observability, #panel-v3-canary
- Related tickets: JIRA-7428 (kernel dispatch investigation), JIRA-7391 (rollout UI quick filters), PR#4120 (dashboard wiring)

Freeform / draft text for runbook (to paste into Confluence)
"When canary delta indicates service degradation (p95 diff > 40% sustained for 5m and traffic > 10rps), the rollout system will auto-pause the canary and create a linked incident. Operators should follow the per-route mitigation checklist: verify KV cache miss rates, inspect topology for cold-starts, and if necessary, trigger model variant fallback via the console. If embedding-similarity drift is detected, run the semantic smoke test before deciding on rollback."

Quick wins for this sprint
- Wire dashboard quick filter (Miguel)
- Staging alerts + ops pager connection (Ravi)
- Runbook text + per-route checklist (Lena)

If blocked: ping Aisha or drop a note in #rollouts-observability.
